skill.name: slack
skill.description: Use browser automation to navigate Slack, search conversations, read unread messages, capture screenshots, and summarize workspace information with user-approved scope.
skill.summary: Automate scoped Slack browsing, search, message review, and evidence capture through agent-browser.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline element references, Slack URLs, and fixed agent-browser examples. One low-severity workspace-specific Slack URL should be sanitized, and the main residual risk is privacy exposure from reading messages and saving Slack screenshots.

remediation.issue: Sensitive Slack message and screenshot handling
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user scope for workspaces, channels, DMs, and time windows. Redact screenshots and summarize messages instead of copying full conversations.

remediation.issue: Workspace-specific Slack URL in reference material
remediation.suggestion: Replace the vercel.slack.com archive example with a generic Slack URL that does not include real workspace, channel, or message identifiers.

remediation.issue: Shell script examples can look executable to scanners
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that shell examples are optional and user-directed. Keep commands fixed to agent-browser and avoid adding user-supplied values to shell execution.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Slack Data Collection
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to read Slack conversations, extract user, message, timestamp, and reaction details, and capture screenshots. This is legitimate for scoped Slack automation but can expose confidential workspace communications if run too broadly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly documents Slack data extraction fields and screenshot capture around user conversations. There is no external exfiltration endpoint, so the concern is scoped privacy exposure rather than malware behavior.

content.value_statement: Slack work often requires manual checks across channels, DMs, search results, and threads. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through browser-based Slack navigation and scoped evidence capture.
actual_capabilities: Connect to an existing browser session or open the Slack web app.
Use accessibility snapshots to locate channels, DMs, tabs, buttons, and message areas.
Check unread activity across Activity, DMs, and channel sidebar views.
Search Slack messages and capture relevant result context.
Extract visible channel, message, user, timestamp, and reaction details.
Capture local screenshots of Slack state for review.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Slack browser session.
Only sees workspaces, channels, and messages available to the signed-in account.
Browser element references change by session and require fresh snapshots.
Screenshots and snapshots can contain sensitive Slack data and need careful handling.

use_cases.title: Review unread activity
use_cases.description: Summarize unread channels and DMs before a team lead starts daily triage.

use_cases.title: Find incident messages
use_cases.description: Search channel history for incident terms, senders, timestamps, and thread context.

use_cases.title: Capture workspace status evidence
use_cases.description: Collect scoped screenshots and visible Slack details for an operations handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Check unread Slack activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect to my Slack browser session, review Activity, DMs, and unread channels, then summarize unread items without opening private DMs unless I ask.

prompt_templates.title: Search one channel
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Slack for the topic I provide in the channel I name. Summarize matching messages with sender, time, channel, and useful context.

prompt_templates.title: Review a thread with evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the Slack conversation I specify, inspect the relevant thread, capture a local screenshot, and summarize the decision, owner, and next step.

prompt_templates.title: Create a scoped workspace report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the approved channels, search terms, and time window I provide. Produce a concise report of findings and list any screenshots saved locally.

output_examples.input: Check my unread Slack activity for work planning.
output: Two DMs show unread badges, but their contents were not opened.
Local screenshots were captured for your review.

output_examples.input: Find messages about the deployment issue in the engineering channel.
output: Several matching messages mention deployment errors and rollback timing.
The main thread includes a proposed fix, owner, and follow-up time.
The summary includes senders, visible timestamps, and channel context.

output_examples.input: Create a handoff summary from the approved incident channels.
output: The report groups findings by channel and topic.
Each item includes visible message context and a recommended follow-up.
Sensitive content is summarized instead of copied in full.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, channels, and DMs before reading message content.
Take fresh snapshots after navigation because element references change.
Redact screenshots or message excerpts before sharing them outside the workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not monitor DMs or private channels without explicit user approval.
Do not reuse old element references across browser sessions.
Do not paste full message archives when a scoped summary is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill use the Slack API?
faq.answer: No. It uses browser automation against the Slack web app and does not require Slack API tokens.

faq.question: Does it require a logged-in Slack session?
faq.answer: Yes. The browser must already be authenticated, or the user must complete Slack sign-in.

faq.question: Can it send Slack messages?
faq.answer: It can interact with the Slack UI when the user requests it. Review message drafts before sending.

faq.question: Can it access private channels?
faq.answer: It can only access channels and DMs visible to the signed-in Slack account.

faq.question: Where are screenshots stored?
faq.answer: Screenshots are saved as local files named by the workflow. Treat them as sensitive workspace records.

faq.question: Is it suitable for confidential workspaces?
faq.answer: Yes, with strict scope. Avoid broad extraction, redact outputs, and confirm before opening private conversations.
